subject: Sizing request: Dedicated capacity for Sapphire NLP assistant
messages:
From: Elaine Rodriguez <elaine.rodriguez@sapphirehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@sapphirehealth.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing request: Dedicated capacity for Sapphire NLP assistant

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get a firm recommendation from Redwood for a dedicated deployment (reserved capacity) that will support our virtual assistant for patient intake and triage. High-level workload below — attaching our hourly traffic CSV (sapphire-traffic-profile.csv).

- Expected daily active users: 60k (US only)
- Peak concurrent sessions: 1,200 (observed in pilot window)
- Typical prompt length (tokens): 60 tokens in user prompt + 120 tokens generated on average
- Target latency SLO: P95 <= 300ms end-to-end for short guidance flows (we can accept higher for long transcripts)
- Expected steady-state qps at peak: approx 55 requests/sec (user requests)
- Business ask: what committed tokens/sec and GPU pool would you recommend, plus headroom for 2x burst? Also need cost estimate (monthly reserved) and any SLA constraints.

Procurement will also need SOC 2 evidence and a short note on data residency controls — I copied procurement.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Rodriguez
Head of Product, AI
Sapphire Health

Attachments: sapphire-traffic-profile.csv (csv, 12 KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Rodriguez <elaine.rodriguez@sapphirehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: Dedicated capacity for Sapphire NLP assistant

Hi Elaine — thanks for the traffic file and the clear SLO. Pasting a short, pragmatic recommendation below; I attached a spreadsheet with the assumptions and per-hour token projection (sapphire-draft-sizing.xlsx).

Summary recommendation (initial committed pool):
- Committed GPU pool: 6x A10G (or 4x H100 equivalent) with 2x burst buffer for busy windows.
- Tokens/sec baseline target to commit: 22k tokens/sec sustained at peak hours.
- Why 22k: 55 req/sec * (60+120 tokens) = 55 * 180 = 9,900 tokens/sec of steady request work; add 1.8x concurrency and overhead (KV cache miss, long-running generations) -> ~18k; round up to 22k to reach P95 headroom and allow some model parallelism.
- Latency assumptions: on A10G we model ~220ms P95 for 180-token responses with batching of 1.2 average; H100 gives ~140–160ms P95 in the same profile. These are conservative (see sheet).
- Headroom plan: reserve 2x burst capacity (auto-burst to shared host fleet) to absorb traffic spikes up to ~44k tokens/sec for short windows.
- Ops/rollout note: start with a canary pool (1 GPU) running the exact model variant, run 48h of traffic replay against the pool, then uplift to committed capacity.

Cost and SLA (ballpark):
- Reserved monthly estimate (6x A10G equivalent): $62,000/mo (includes reserved pool + management + 99.9% infra SLA).
- Optional H100 pack (4x): ~$95,000/mo (lower latency, fewer nodes).

Next actions I suggest:
1) Confirm which GPU family you prefer (A10G cost-optimized vs H100 low-latency).
2) Confirm whether the 2x burst buffer is acceptable under your cost model.
3) We'll run a traffic replay on a canary image; need a signed NDA + access token (I can share a HubSpot link with the PO).

Will drop the sizing sheet in Drive and open a short call to walk the math if helpful.

— Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sapphire-draft-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42 KB)
Related: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/8341

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Rodriguez <elaine.rodriguez@sapphirehealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: Dedicated capacity for Sapphire NLP assistant

Hi Elaine — quick commercial note to accompany Soojin's technical sizing:

- If Sapphire opts for the 12-month reserved commitment at the recommended 22k tokens/sec baseline we can offer a 12% commitment discount and include 48-hour SLA for incident response.
- If you need stricter latency SLAs (P95 <= 200ms), we'll recommend the H100 configuration and can structure a blended pricing option to reduce step-up cost.

Can you confirm whether procurement prefers a firm committed tokens/sec (for contract language) or a tiered commit model (e.g., commit to a minimum of 15k tokens/sec with a shared burst pool up to 44k)? Procurement often requests the tiered approach for flexibility.

Thanks — cc'ing solutions and infra.
— Vanessa
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sizing request: Dedicated capacity for Sapphire NLP assistant

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement and product: 

1) Procurement: please attach SOC 2 evidence and the data residency statement. We attached our questionnaire; feel free to answer inline. (See procurement-questionnaire.pdf)

2) Product: we prefer the tiered commit model (min 15k tokens/sec committed, burst to 44k). Can you confirm the expected P95 latency at 15k vs 22k on A10G, and the delta if we move to H100? Also want to understand degraded-mode behavior if burst capacity is exhausted — will the system fail open to a lower-capacity model or queue requests?

3) Ops ask: can you provide the timeline for the canary replay and what logs/artifacts we get (traces, token counts, per-request latency histograms)? We need this to be part of the acceptance criteria.

If you can reply with the P95 numbers and acceptance checklist I can push this through legal and procurement next week.

Best,
Elaine
